labels.og_answer: The largest just under 14 m (46 ft), by a model

top.answer: The largest adults of Spinosaurus aegyptiacus were just under 14 m (46 ft) long and about 7.4 tonnes, by a model of 2022. Nobody has found a whole skeleton. Ours is a young one, about 10 m (33 ft), about three quarters of full size, about 3 to 4 tonnes, a model's figure. Beside the person of 1.70 m, its hip joint sits at about head height, and it is almost six people long.
top.answer_more: Against T. rex: the largest Spinosaurus was longer, most likely lighter and much lower at the hips. The two never met, about 30 million years and two continents apart.

scale.what: Our Spinosaurus beside a person 1.70 m tall, to one scale: a young one of about 10 m (33 ft), built on the skeleton from Morocco. The pale outline behind it is the largest adults' size by the model of 2022, just under 14 m (46 ft): our model enlarged by about a third. The outline is an estimate, not an animal anyone found.

close.what: The head and the front of the body, closer up, with the person. The snout is long and narrow, the teeth are cones without a saw edge, the nostrils sit far back. The low crest in front of the eyes is certain, its height is not: its top edge is broken on every piece found. The lips are a choice, not a find.

guess.q: How old was the young animal from Morocco when it died?
guess.a: About 17 years, by the growth rings in its thigh bone, give or take two years. It was not full grown, at about three quarters of the size of the largest adults.

blocks.nav: Spinosaurus vs T. rex, size only
blocks.h: Spinosaurus vs T. rex, size only
paras: The largest Spinosaurus was longer than any T. rex: just under 14 m (46 ft) by a model, against about 12 m (39 ft) for SUE's skeleton. It was most likely not heavier: about 7.4 to 8 tonnes in the model, against about 8 to 9 tonnes for the largest known T. rex. At the hips it stood much lower: the thigh bone of the young animal from Morocco is 61 cm, SUE's is 1.32 m. The two never met, Spinosaurus lived about 95 million years ago in North Africa, T. rex about 68 to 66 million years ago in North America. A comparison of size, nothing more.

scale.what: Our Spinosaurus and our T. rex, to one scale on one ground line. Our Spinosaurus is a young one of about 10 m (33 ft), our T. rex after SUE a large adult of about 11.4 m (37 ft), so the T. rex is the longer one here. An adult Spinosaurus was longer than any T. rex, most likely lighter and much lower at the hips.

Our T. rex, after SUE, about 11.4 m

paras: It stood and walked on two legs, its weight over the hind feet, its arms carrying none of it. The four-legged animal of 2014 rested on a sum that added the air inside the body instead of taking it away. One of its own authors reported that in 2024.

The tail was deep and flat from side to side, like a blade: tall spines above, long bones below. We know that from the own tail bones of the animal from Morocco, about four fifths of the tail was found. What it was for is argued: swimming or display.

The spines are known, the tallest on Stromer's skeleton about 1.65 m (5.4 ft) of bone. The shape of the sail above them nobody knows, so our plain arc is our choice. A thin skin over the spines is the most likely reading, and most specialists read the sail as display.

The snout was long and narrow, widened at the tip like a spoon, with cone-shaped teeth without a saw edge and small nostrils far back. In front of the eyes sat a low crest, its top edge broken on every piece found. Skin, lips and colour are known from no spinosaur, so our colours are ours.

It lived by the water and ate fish, as its teeth and the isotopes in them show. Whether it chased the fish swimming, or waded and waited for them in the shallows, is argued. The case for swimming rests on the deep tail of 2020 and the dense bones in a study of 2022. Most of the work since 2021 points to wading. Models find it too buoyant to dive, its skull shape fits an ambush hunter, and the bone-density method was criticised as unreliable in 2024. The museums keep the question open, and so do we.

In the autumn of 1912 the first bones came to light in the Bahariya Oasis in Egypt. They were the lower jaw's front half, 72 cm long, and back, hip and tail bones with the tall spines of the sail. Stromer described them in 1915 and named the animal Spinosaurus after those spines. It was a young one, about the size of ours. The skeleton stood in Munich and was destroyed in a bombing raid in 1944. Only Stromer's notes, drawings and a few photographs survive. Munich holds a Spinosaurus tooth today, not a skeleton.

In 2008 a collector found the first bones near Zrigat in south-eastern Morocco, in the Kem Kem beds. The site was dug out in 2013, the tail from 2015 to 2019. Since 2014 this skeleton has been the species' new type, because Stromer's bones are gone. It is kept in Casablanca, at the Faculté des Sciences Aïn Chock.

points: The hips on both sides, both legs, an ankle bone and a nearly complete foot.
The tail, more than 30 bones, about four fifths of its length.
Parts of neck, back and hip bones, pieces of rib, pieces of the skull and one finger bone.
The spines of the sail and the lower jaw: after Stromer's lost skeleton.
The snout: after the adult snout in Milan, scaled down.
The back of the skull, the arms and the hands: after the relatives Irritator, Suchomimus and Baryonyx.
The neck, most of the back, the ribs, the shoulder and the end of the tail: after other finds, or restored.

end: So every reconstruction is one animal made of several, ours too.

paras: Three things decide every number on this page.

points: Every adult length is a model:

nobody has an adult skeleton. The researchers took the young skeleton from Morocco and enlarged it by about a third, until it fitted the largest snout found. The snout is a real fossil, the body around it is a sum.
The weight comes from a body model:

build flesh around the skeleton, measure the volume, multiply by a density. For Spinosaurus the air spaces in the neck and body alone move the answer by 600 kg, 7.4 to 8 tonnes in one and the same model.
our animal is a young one of about 10 m. Its numbers are its own, never the species'. That is why three numbers stand apart here: our animal, the largest adults by the model, and Stromer's skeleton.

blocks.intro: For each number: where it came from, and what it means.

rows.text: A figure of 2005: a whole body was drawn around the big snout in Milan, with the build of a long-legged relative. Spinosaurus turned out to have short legs, so that body came out too long. The model of 2022 gives just under 14 m, though some museum texts still give 18 m.
The digital skeleton of 2014, scaled up to adult size. The same team's better model of 2022 came out more than a metre shorter.

A sum of 2007 that went from the skull's length to the body, with a formula built on other meat-eating dinosaurs: a shorter and much heavier animal. We have not read the study's exact range ourselves, and the body model of 2022 gives the largest adults 7.4 to 8 tonnes.
The current model, about 7.4 tonnes for the largest adults, 7.4 to 8 by the air spaces chosen. It does not apply to our young one, which comes to about 3 to 4 tonnes.
No. Spinosaurus is the longest meat-eating dinosaur known. In the sea, megalodon was longer, at about 16 m (52 ft). T. rex was most likely heavier, and it certainly stood higher at the hips.
The study of 2014, by a sum of where the body's weight sat. The sum added the air inside the body instead of taking it away, as one of its own authors reported in 2024.
A headline of 2020 about the newly found tail. The study itself calls the tail an organ of propulsion, and most work since reads the animal as an ambush hunter in the shallows. Argued, not settled.

blocks.nav: Why our Spinosaurus looks like this
blocks.h: Why our Spinosaurus looks like this
paras: It is built to the measurements of the bones of the young animal from Morocco, hips, legs, foot and tail at their sizes. Where its own bones are missing, it follows Stromer's skeleton and relatives. The arc of the sail and the colours are our choice, because neither the sail's shape nor any colour is known. It stands on two legs, arms raised, neck in a gentle curve, and runs about 10 m (33 ft) in this pose.

items.a: Our young one: the top of the sail about 3.5 m (11.5 ft), the head about 3 m (9.7 ft) in its pose. Its hip joint sits about 1.6 m (5.2 ft) up. For adults no hip height is published, only that T. rex stood higher at the hips.

No, it was the longest known meat-eater among the dinosaurs. The long-necked dinosaurs were far bigger: Argentinosaurus about 30 to 35 m (98 to 115 ft) long and roughly 65 to 80 tonnes. More on the biggest dinosaurs page.
